W2 (empirical), after E019. Tip is E017: 6.548 s, 0.7537, only ~0.07 pp above the 0.753 bar.

Measured: E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 -0.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E009 LR floor 0 0.7564. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E012 rerun of E010 bit-identical. E013 LS0.2 0.7551. E014 Muon lr x1.5 0.7557. E015 CUDA graphs 0.7574/6.578. E016 wd/2 0.7607/6.58. E017 break-free 0.7537/6.548. E018 24/32 only 0.7502/5.99. E019 (E016 code at dddcf96 rerun) 0.7541/6.54.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: -0.5 epoch costs ~0.18 pp and saves ~4.8% time, roughly linear (E007->E008). True epochs are probably ~0.5 more than labelled.
2. EMA/Lookahead: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s, the cheapest gain.
3. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s.
4. Time tracks pixel count/FLOPs. Dropping the 28 px phase cost -0.72 pp for -8.5% time. Cutting res costs ~0.085 pp per 1% of time, worse than epochs (~0.04).
5. Width 576->512: -4.8% time, -0.25 pp.
6. LS, Muon lr, LR floor and wd are flat within noise. E019 shows the E016 gain was noise: the same recipe under a different build/compile gave 0.7541 vs 0.7607.
7. CUDA graphs and break removal give ~1% each. The run is compute-bound.
8. Noise: a rerun of identical code is bit-identical, but a math-identical edit reshuffles the 3-seed mean by up to ±0.4 pp. Time noise is ~0.5%. The tip's true mean is ~0.754-0.755.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and E016 (noise), and over-predicted E009, E011 and E018. Lesson: every cut costs 0.04-0.09 pp per 1% time, margin is ~0.07 pp, so no trim is affordable. Accuracy-neutral knobs are unresolvable below ~0.4 pp.

Unsure: whether any free gain exists, and how far the tip's true mean sits above 0.753.

forecasts.reason: -1 true epoch saves ~5-9% time but costs ~0.2-0.4 pp from a 0.07 pp margin; likely falls under 0.753.
Narrowing a 51%-of-MACs group costs accuracy like the width-512 cut (~0.25 pp for 4.8%); margin is gone.
wd effects flat within noise (E019 undid E016's gain); expected gain is ~0 with ±0.4 pp reshuffle.
Removing a conv at the highest-res stage saves ~5% time and costs depth accuracy; likely below the bar.
E011 and E018 show low-res time cuts cost ~0.085 pp per 1% time; 20 px phase of 15% saves ~3% for ~0.25 pp.

cruxes: What is the tip's true mean accuracy over many seeds: is it ~0.754 or ~0.757? That decides whether any trim is affordable.
Does any time-neutral accuracy gain exist (BN recalibration, EMA variants) that exceeds the ±0.4 pp reshuffle noise?
Are per-seed results stable across fresh builds (inductor autotune), i.e. is 0.7537 vs 0.7607 a build artifact?
